content: Wheat is a rabi crop grown from October to March in India. Major growing states are Punjab, Haryana, Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh. MSP for wheat 2024-25 is Rs 2275 per quintal. Best selling season is April-May after harvest. Wheat prices typically rise in October-November due to sowing demand. Store wheat below 12% moisture. Key mandis: Hapur, Narela, Khanna. Average yield: 40-50 quintals per acre.

Onion is grown in kharif and rabi seasons. Maharashtra produces 40% of India's onions. Key mandi: Lasalgaon APMC is Asia's largest onion market. Onion prices are highly volatile — can swing 50-200% within weeks. Best selling window is 2-3 months post harvest. MSP not fixed but government intervenes via NAFED. Storage in cool dry place extends shelf life 3-4 months. Typical price range Rs 800-3500 per quintal. Export bans affect prices significantly.

Tomato is a high-value perishable crop. Cannot be stored beyond 7-10 days. Prices are extremely seasonal — crash to Rs 100/quintal in peak season and spike to Rs 2000+ in off-season. Major markets: Kolar (Karnataka), Nashik (Maharashtra). Sell within 3 days of harvest. Cold chain reduces losses significantly. Monsoon disruption causes major price spikes. Do not hold tomatoes — always sell immediately.

Cotton is a kharif crop harvested October-February. MSP for cotton 2024-25: Rs 7121 per quintal (long staple), Rs 6620 (medium staple). Major states: Gujarat, Maharashtra, Telangana. Cotton can be stored 6-12 months safely. Prices improve November-January. CCI (Cotton Corporation of India) procures at MSP. Export demand from China affects prices. Avoid selling in October — wait for November-December for better prices.

Soybean is a kharif oilseed crop. MSP 2024-25: Rs 4892 per quintal. Major growing states: Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Rajasthan. Harvest: October-November. Prices typically softer at harvest and firm up January onwards. Safe storage for 6 months in dry conditions. NAFED and state agencies procure at MSP. Export demand affects prices. Processing demand from soyoil and soy meal industry.

Rice (Paddy) is a kharif staple crop. MSP for common paddy 2024-25: Rs 2300 per quintal. Major states: West Bengal, Punjab, Uttar Pradesh, Andhra Pradesh. Harvested October-December. Government procurement through FCI at MSP. Basmati rice commands premium — Rs 3500-6000/quintal. Store paddy below 14% moisture for 12+ months. Export demand for basmati is strong. Sell to government procurement centers for guaranteed MSP.

Maize is grown in both kharif and rabi seasons. MSP 2024-25: Rs 2225 per quintal. Major states: Karnataka, Madhya Pradesh, Bihar. Poultry feed industry drives 60% demand. Prices improve April-June. Ethanol blending policy boosting demand significantly. Store in dry conditions for 6 months. Key buyers: NAFED, poultry companies, starch industries.

Potato is a rabi vegetable crop. No fixed MSP but state governments intervene. Major states: Uttar Pradesh, West Bengal, Bihar. Cold storage essential — extends shelf life 6-8 months. Prices crash during March-April harvest; improve August-September. Processing demand from chips and fry industry growing. Sell 40% at harvest, store 60% for August-September when prices are 2x higher. Key mandis: Agra, Aligarh, Farrukhabad.

PM-KISAN Yojana: Central government scheme providing Rs 6000 per year direct income support to farmer families in three equal installments of Rs 2000. Eligible: All landholding farmer families. Exclusions: Income taxpayers, government employees, professionals. How to apply: PM-KISAN portal or Common Service Centers. Documents: Aadhaar, land records, bank account.

MSP (Minimum Support Price): Government announces MSP for 23 crops every year. Key crops: Wheat Rs 2275, Rice Rs 2300, Cotton Rs 6620-7121, Soybean Rs 4892, Maize Rs 2225 (2024-25). Procurement through FCI, NAFED, CCI, state agencies. Farmer must register at nearest procurement center with land records and Aadhaar. Payment via DBT within 72 hours of sale.

PMFBY (Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana): Crop insurance scheme. Premium: 2% for kharif, 1.5% for rabi, 5% for horticulture. Coverage: Natural calamities, pests, disease. How to claim: Inform within 72 hours of crop loss. Apply through banks, CSC, or PMFBY portal. Maximum claim based on sum insured per crop per district.

When is the best time to sell crops? For perishable crops (tomato, onion, leafy vegetables) — sell within 3-7 days of harvest. For cereals (wheat, rice, maize) — monitor MSP and mandi prices weekly for 30-60 days post harvest. For cash crops (cotton, soybean) — prices generally improve 2-3 months after harvest. Always compare: current mandi price vs storage cost vs price trend before deciding to hold or sell.

How to choose the best mandi? Compare: distance vs transport cost vs price difference. Generally price difference should be 5-10% higher to justify extra 50 km travel. Check: AGMARKNET website for daily prices across mandis. Consider: Auction system reputation, payment terms (same day vs 3-day), facilities at mandi. Register at mandi using Aadhaar and land records before selling.

When should you store vs sell immediately? Store when: Current prices are at seasonal low, uptrend detected in last 7-14 days, you have quality storage facility, crop can be safely stored (cereals 6-12 months, pulses 6-9 months). Sell immediately when: Crop is perishable (tomato, leafy), monsoon approaching which may damage stock, you need immediate cash, prices showing consistent downtrend for 14+ days.

Market trends in Indian agriculture follow seasonal patterns. Prices typically fall during harvest season (kharif: Oct-Nov, rabi: Mar-Apr) due to supply glut. Prices rise during lean season (opposite of harvest). Export bans cause immediate domestic price crashes. Weather shocks (drought, floods) in major producing regions cause 20-50% price spikes within 2 weeks. EMA-7 crossing above EMA-14 signals short-term uptrend. Consistent EMA-30 uptrend with 3+ weeks of rising prices indicates strong bull market.

Farm profit calculation: Net Profit = Revenue - (Seed Cost + Fertilizer + Pesticide + Labour + Irrigation + Transport + Packaging + Market Cess). Typical cost breakdown per acre for wheat: Seed Rs 1500, Fertilizer Rs 3000, Labour Rs 4000, Irrigation Rs 2000, Transport Rs 800, Total Cost ~Rs 12000, Revenue at MSP: Rs 2275 x 45 quintal = Rs 102375, Net Profit ~Rs 90375 per acre. Track all expenses from sowing to selling for accurate profit calculation.

Weather impact on agriculture and crop prices: Deficit monsoon (less than 90% of normal) — expect 10-20% price rise for kharif crops. Excess rain during harvest — quality damage, prices may fall 5-10% due to moisture content issues. Cold wave during rabi — wheat yields improve, prices stable. Hailstorm — localized damage, immediate price spike in that region. El Nino years — typically below normal monsoon — bullish for most agricultural commodities.
